sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Death Lightning** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
- Trade the Remembrance of the Lichdragon, gained by defeating Lichdragon Fortissax, with Finger Reader Enia.
- Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown:
Sends out Lightning bolts that hit randomly around the caster, inflict 50 Death Blight build-up and hit with Attack Power equal to 513% of Incantation Scaling, and leave behind clouds inflicting 30 of Death Blight build-up every 0.2 seconds for 3 seconds (450 build-up in total from the clouds).

Charging this spell sends out more bolts over a larger area and increases the Attack Power of them to 564% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Casting the spell costs 32 points of Stamina. Charging the spell increases the cost to 42 points of Stamina.
- Deals 5 Stance damage per hit. Charging the spell increases this to 9.25 Stance damage per hit.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
 - Since charging the spell already increases Attack Power by 9.9%, wearing this talisman increases the Attack Power by a total of 26%.
- Attack Power is boosted by 15% per Gravel Stone Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Attack Power is boosted by 2% per piece of the Death Knight Set that is being worn.
- This spell is notoriously unreliable, capable of dealing great damage but hitting only rarely against smaller foes and being fairly inaccurate even against massive bosses.
 - Generally outclassed by Ancient Dragons' Lightning Strike, though that spell is acquired a good bit later.
- This spell sometimes fails to do anything when cast under low-level roofs.

sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.07: Decreased FP consumption.
 - FP cost was decreased from 32 to 28.
- Patch 1.04: Decreased FP cost, Increased the duration of death-accumulating smoke.
 - FP cost was decreased from 46 to 32.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Discus of Light** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Golden Order Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Purchase:** Roundtable Hold / Altus Plateau / Leyndell, Royal Capital / Mountaintops of the Giants
- Sold for 11,000 Runes by Brother Corhyn after he moves to Goldmask's location in Altus.
- Should Corhyn die before purchasing this incantation after moving to Goldmask's location, then the player can still purchase it from the Twin Maiden Husks for the same price after giving them Corhyn's Bell Bearing.
 - WARNING: If Corhyn dies before this incantation appears in his inventory then it will become unavailable for that character until a new Journey is started.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Throws out a ring of light with Holy Attack Power equal to 150% of Incantation Scaling and going through foes, stopping when it reaches its maximum range or hits an object.

The ring begins to return to the caster shortly after arriving at its destination, having the same Attack Power for its attack against all foes it passes through.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast.
- Attack Power is boosted by 10% per Golden Order Seal held in an active hand (2 max) and by 15% per Dryleaf Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
 - Since it's possible to acquire both of these Seals in one Playthrough, it's one of a few spells able to stack Seal boosts (for a total boost of 27% in this case).
- Wearing the Radiant Gold Mask increases Attack Power by 10%.
- Effectively has Attack Power roughly equal to 300% of Incantation Scaling per cast since it will very often hit the main target on the way back.
- Several rings can be out at the same time, making the spell very spammable.
- Pairs well with the Erdtree Greatshield's skill Golden Retaliation and the Ash of War: Carian Retaliation since the timing of the returning ring is very predictable and will trigger the spell-parry-into-projectile part of those skills.
- Can be cast while riding Torrent, further extending the incantation's usability and ability to be spammed.
- The caster takes a short step forwards each time the spell is cast. While many steep falls prevent a character from stepping over them from movement caused by Skills, Spells, and Weapons, it's still good to be a bit careful.
- Though it goes through all enemies it will not ignore the damage reduction from an enemy that is keeping its guard up if they are guarding in the direction it's flying from.
 - Note that it will still fly through said guarding enemy and will hit their unprotected back when returning unless said enemy turns around in between the two hits.

sections.markdown:

 - Decreased FP cost from 9 to 3.
- Patch 1.04 decreased FP cost, increased damage, and cast speed.
 - Decreased FP cost from 11 to 9. Attack Power was increased from 114% of Incantation Scaling to 150% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Dragonbolt Blessing** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Cult Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Loot:** Altus Plateau
- Dragonbolt Blessing is found in a treasure chest within Stormcaller Church.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown: Summons a crackling aura that increases the resistance to all Status Effects by 30 and causes the one-handed light attacks of non-Great or Colossal weapons to be deflected. This also reduces the caster's Lightning Damage Negation by 35% and counts as a Body Buff, and lasts for 70 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast.
- Deflects the one-handed regular light attacks of Daggers, Throwing Blades Shadow of the Erdtree, Straight Swords, Thrusting Swords, Heavy Thrusting Swords, Curved Swords, Backhand Blades, Katanas, Great Katanas Shadow of the Erdtree, Twinblades, Axes, Spears, the Bloodfiend's Sacred Spear Shadow of the Erdtree Great Spear, Halberds, Reapers, the Katar and Pata Shadow of the Erdtree Fists, Claws, and Beast Claws Shadow of the Erdtree.
 - Unarmed attacks are also deflected.
 - One-handed regular light attacks from Staves, Sacred Seals, Torches, and Small Shields are also deflected.
 - Fists besides the Katar and Pata aren't deflected.
 - For Daggers, Thrusting Swords (except the Estoc and Noble's Estoc, where regular heavy attacks aren't deflectable), Heavy Thrusting Swords (except the Sword Lance Shadow of the Erdtree, where regular heavy attacks aren't deflectable), Twinblades, Axes (except the Iron Cleaver and Celebrant's Cleaver, where regular heavy attacks aren't deflectable), Spears, the Bloodfiend's Sacred Spear, Reapers, the Katar and Pata, Claws, and Beast Claws, one-handed regular heavy attacks and running light attacks are also deflected.
 - For Katanas, running light attacks are also deflected.
 - For Light Greatswords Shadow of the Erdtree, one-handed regular heavy attacks are actually deflected.
 - For Thrusting Swords, running heavy attacks, rolling light attacks, and backstep light attacks are also deflected.
 - For Heavy Thrusting Swords, rolling light attacks and backstep light attacks are also deflected.
- Combines well with the Skill: Raptor of the Mists since that skill will also make the user dodge an attack that would have hit them, thus preventing the damage, while the slight stun of the Dragonbolt Blessing can make it easier to land the attack.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - This incantation actually deflects all weapon attacks with an AttackRepel value below 70.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Dragonice** is an incantation spell in Elden Ring. It is one of the Dragon Communion Incantations.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown:
Dragon Communion:** Caelid / Jagged Peak
- Acquired from the altar at the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for 1 Dragon Heart.

sections.heading: Effects
sections.markdown:
Creates a dragon head, before breathing out a wave of frozen mist, dealing Magic damage equal to 135% of Incantation Scaling and inflicting 110 Frostbite build-up up to 3 times (i.e. damage for 405% of the same and 330 Frostbite build-up cumulatively) if the entire wave hits.

Continue channeling the spell to let loose a second breath, also hitting up to 3 times.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 48 points of Stamina to cast, and another 48 points upon using the follow-up breath.
- Damage is boosted by 10% by the Roar Medallion.
- Damage is boosted by 15% per Dragon Communion Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
- Damage is boosted by 20% when the Rock Heart is used.
- This spell can be cast while mounted but cannot be cast in midair, unlike Borealis's Mist and Ghostflame Breath.
- Of the three Frostbite-causing Dragon Breaths (this spell, Borealis's Mist, and Ghostflame Breath), this is the most cost-effective for inflicting Frostbite, but causes less damage than the other two breaths.
 - Compared to Borealis's Mist, this spell deals 15% less damage but also consumes 29% less FP.
 - Compared to Ghostflame Breath, this spell deals 20% less damage but consumes 17% less FP and causes 100% more Frostbite build-up.
- Casting this spell until it stops costs 120 FP: 2*36 FP from the two breaths and 12*4 FP from keeping the spell running.
 - Only 65 FP is actually needed for the entire routine. This is just enough to start the second breath and thereafter the game does not care that no FP remains as it will continue casting regardless.
- This is the second weakest "default" dragon breath attack, dealing 15% less damage than Glintstone Breath and 6% less damage than Dragonfire (the latter is only if an enemy's Fire Damage Negation and Magic Damage Negation is equal), and deals only 3% more damage than Rotten Breath.
 - However, the Frostbite build-up of the spell can even the field against non-immune enemies as it deals a significant amount of percentage-based damage and lowers their Damage Negation against further attacks.
- Deals 20% less damage against other players.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.07 the power of the following incantations in PvP has been decreased.
 - The multiplier for damage against other players was lowered from 100% to 80%.

sections.heading: See also
sections.markdown:
- Borealis's Mist, a stronger but more expensive version of this spell
- Dragonfire, a slightly stronger Fire damage version of this spell
- Ghostflame Breath, a version of this spell with higher Magic damage but lower Frostbite build-up
- Glintstone Breath, a stronger Magic damage version of this spell with no Frostbite build-up
- Rotten Breath, a slightly weaker Standard damage of this spell that also inflicts Scarlet Rot

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
D, Hunter of the Dead** is an NPC in *Elden Ring.*

He is also possible to summon as a cooperator in Black Knife Catacombs.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Darian, more commonly known as D, Hunter of the Dead is an undead hunter and an ally of Gurranq, the Beast Clergyman. Darian has a twin brother by the name of Devin, who was also called D. While Darian and Devin had different minds and bodies, they shared a single soul, and were reviled as cursed beings. The twins found sanctuary in the Golden Order, the only institution to accept them.

Darian befriended the spellblade Rogier, with whom he shared an interest in Those Who Live in Death. The two friends eventually parted ways, each coming to their own conclusion about the undead.

Darian became a proponent of Golden Order fundamentalism and a hunter of Those Who Live in Death, seeking to stamp out defilement and preserve the perfection of the Golden Order. Darian encountered and became an ally of Gurranq, who bid him to weed out Deathroot, a plant which caused the emergence of Those Who Live in Death, so that he might feed it to him.

Following the traces of death, Darian came upon Summonwater Village, where a Tibia Mariner had set up shop. In the outskirts of the village, he encounters a Tarnished champion and warns them to stay away from the village. After the champion defeats the Mariner and weeds out the Deathroot, Darian offers them a deal; to take his place as Gurranq's servant, in exchange for Gurranq sharing with them the strength of beasts.

With other matters to attend to, Darian relocates to Roundtable Hold. After the Tarnished takes him up on his offer, he declares them brothers-in-arms and teaches them the fundamentalist techniques wielded by the hunters of the dead. Another resident of Roundtable Hold and associate of the Tarnished champion is Fia, a deathbed companion and servant of the Prince of Death. Fia gives the Tarnished a dagger, asking them to find its rightful owner. After the Tarnished shows Darian the dagger, he offers to return it to its owner.

Shortly thereafter, Darian is murdered by Fia. The Tarnished champion may retrieve Darian's armor and find his twin. Devin will don the armor, and avenge his brother, finding Fia at the foot of the Prince of Death and murdering her.

sections.heading: Questline Progression
sections.markdown:
1. Limgrave
 - *(Optional)* D can first be encountered close to Saintsbridge in Limgrave. He will warn you about Summonwater Village, which is overrun by Those Who Live in Death, including a Tibia Mariner.
 - *(Optional)* After defeating the Tibia Mariner in Summonwater Village, D will appear appear in the village and offer to introduce you to Gurranq.
1. Roundtable Hold
 - D will appear in Roundtable Hold regardless of whether he was encountered in Limgrave. If you have at least one Deathroot and did not complete step 1, he will offer to introduce you to Gurranq.
 - D will begin selling Incantations after you have met Gurranq. He will also become available as a cooperator in Black Knight Catacombs as well as against the Tibia Mariner in Liurnia of the Lakes.
 - After progressing Fia's questline, the Weathered Dagger can be given to D.
 - After reloading the area, Fia can be found standing over D's corpse in a previously inaccessible room in Roundtable Hold.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
The **Dragoncrest Shield Talisman** is a talisman in Elden Ring.

It gives +10% physical damage reduction. This talisman has 4 variants, including Dragoncrest Greatshield Talisman, only one of which can be equipped at a time.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: - Obtained from a corpse that lies on the ground, near Bestial Sanctum, in northern Greyoll's Dragonbarrow. Equipping the Longtail Cat Talisman here, or using Soft Cotton is very helpful, as there are several parkour drops coming up that will deal unavoidable damage, and there are Bat enemies in the area. From the front door of the sanctum, head southwest around the side of the sanctum, until reaching a cliff that overlooks a large tree root, close enough to drop to. Drop from here to the branch, to another branch, to a domed rooftop, and then to the first of 3 ring structures, jutting out from the cliffside. Jump up to the ledge surrounding the nearby pillar, walk across the buttress to the next pillar, drop to the lower ledge, jump to another lower ledge on the first pillar, and drop down to the second ring. Jump to the next-lower ledge on the outer pillar, walk across the buttress, and jump to a ledge that sticks out from the wall below. At this point, it is recommended to mount Torrent, as the final jump is extremely difficult to make on foot, while almost trivial to make with Torrent's double-jump ability. The third ring below is just barely beyond the instant-death threshold for falling, so instead, aim for the ledge on that outer pillar, just a few feet above the ring. After finally reaching the third ring, head northeast along it to find the corpse.

Crucible Feather Talisman** is a talisman in Elden Ring.

Increases the effectiveness of dodge-rolling, but also reduces damage negation, increasing damage taken by 30%.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: - Obtained from a corpse in Auriza Hero's Grave in the Leyndell, Royal Capital region. Make your way to the area where two chariots ride side-by-side, up and down a slope. At the bottom of this slope is a corpse, hanging off of a ledge above a pit. Drop into the pit from where this corpse lies to land on a beam, and continue dropping down into this pit, until landing on the top of a thin stone archway. Walk to the end of this archway and climb a ladder to reach another ramp, guarded by a single chariot. While it is possible to reach the bottom of this ramp without dying, it is extremely difficult, as it involves either taking a hit from the chariot without dying, or using a movement ability, like Bloodhound Step, along with excellent timing. The far easier thing to do is to proceed up the ramp until reaching a moving, fire-breathing pillar, which can be raised by hitting it. After raising the pillar, die or teleport to return to the ramp with two chariots. The raised pillar will now be shining a chariot-spawning circle of light onto the middle of this ramp, which will cause a chariot to spawn that collides with the others, destroying them all. The door at the bottom of the ramp leading to the corpse can now be safely reached.

sections.markdown: The **Deathbird** is a recurring boss in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
All Deathbirds are said to be the offspring of an entity called the twinbird, which is an envoy of an outer god of Death. In the time when there was no Erdtree, Death was burned in ghostflame, and the Deathbirds were the keepers of that fire. They were graveyard fire keepers and were said to rake out the ashen remains of the dead from their kiln. From the cinders of the dead burned with ghostflame arose vengeful spirits. The Deathbirds were regarded as malevolent deities by some. Through the ancient act of the rite of Death, servants of Death were permitted to come among the Deathbirds and become their guardians. This act serves as an oath sworn to their distant resurrection. Such priests can be seen inside the wings of the Death Rite Birds as spirit beings wielding Death ritual spears.

These recurring optional bosses only appear at night, descending from the sky. They are gigantic decaying birds with bodies composed of smaller corpses. They count as Those Who Live in Death despite predating the Deathroot.

sections.heading: Combat Overview
sections.markdown:
- Stance: 120
- This boss is vulnerable to a Critical Attack after its Stance is broken.
- Cannot be Parried
- Vulnerable to effects that target Those Who Live in Death
- Weak spot: Head

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.markdown: Deathbirds usually rely on melee attacks, which can be either dodged or blocked, except for their peck and grab attacks. It's recommended to avoid being under its head to avoid getting pecked.

sections.heading: Background

sections.markdown: Crumbling Farum Azula** is a subregion of the Lands Between in Elden Ring. This legacy dungeon is accessible after burning the Erdtree at the Forge of the Giants found on Flame Peak in the Mountaintops of the Giants.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Farum Azula is a giant temple in the sky, located above the sea to the east of the Lands Between. Once a royal city of the Ancient Dragons and the seat of the Dragonlord Placidusax, Farum Azula has been crumbling since time immemorial. Now, all that remains is a mausoleum guarded by chosen Beastmen, who wield weapons clad in Red Lightning. The storm beyond time rages in the center of the crumbling city, and at its heart is the Dragonlord's seat, where he awaits the return of his god.

In Farum Azula, many Ancient Dragons can be found buried in the rock, between the catacombs of the Beastmen and the surface of the city, their bodies still filled with gold. It is said that they formed a living wall of rock to protect the Dragonlord long ago.

As well as Beastmen, Farum Azula is still home to a number of Ancient Dragons, who roost on the floating fragments of the city. There is also a population of Wormfaces dwelling in one of the lower levels of the city. It appears that Deathroot has spread throughout parts of the city as well.

Farum Azula is the dwelling place of Maliketh, the Black Blade, the protector of the Rune of Death. It is here that the Tarnished finds themselves after the Erdtree is set aflame, and where they finally unbind the Rune of Death, releasing it upon the Lands Between.

Below the Prince of Death's Throne, a nameless Eternal City lies in ruins, with many of its buildings sinking into a mire of milky liquid. In the northwestern area, a Wandering Mausoleum prowls, surrounded by Mausoleum Soldiers and Knights. To the far west, Siluria, one of the two leaders of the Crucible Knights, awaits at the hollowed-out trunk of a dead oak tree.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The Nameless Eternal City was destroyed by Astel, Naturalborn of the Void long ago.

After Godwyn the Golden was murdered on the Night of Black Knives, his body was buried in the Erdtree's roots. His malformed body, corrupted by Death, can be found to the north of the cavern. It is here that Fia resides after fleeing Roundtable Hold.

sections.heading: Acquisition

Alternatively, use one of the Wandering Mausoleums to duplicate one (can only obtain one per playthrough using either method).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- This weapon's Guard Counters become Thrusting Counterattacks.
- Has a 30% damage boost against Dragons and a 15% damage boost against Ancient Dragons.
 - Since this weapon primarily deals Pierce-type damage, which is most dragons weakness, it is well suited to this anti-dragon role. Be aware that Borealis, the Freezing Fog, is a Pierce-resistant dragon and that all Ancient Dragons resist the secondary Lightning damage.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Devin, more commonly known as "D", is the twin-brother of Darian, who is also known as D. The two twins had separate minds and bodies, but shared a single soul. For this, they were reviled as accursed beings, but found solace in the Golden Order, which accepted them both.

At some point, Devin traveled deep below ground to the roots of the Erdtree, where he met with the Prince of Death. The encounter appears to have nearly shattered Devin's mind, as he came to dwell in the Siofra Aqueduct, barely able to speak.

Later, his brother Darian is murdered by Fia, Deathbed Companion, and his Twinned Set finds its way to Devin. Seemingly acknowledging that Darian had died, but still barely able to speak, Devin gathers himself, and if requested, helps the Tarnished champion clear the way to the Deeproot Depths.

After Fia is given the other half of the Cursemark of Death, allowing her to lay with the Prince of Death in order to produce a Mending Rune, Devin will finally find her, and kill her. The Tarnished champion can find Devin gloating and taunting the Prince of Death, cursing him and the murdered Fia. Having avenged his brother, Devin declares he has no more regrets and prays for the honeyed rays of gold to deliver his spirit, so that he may once again look his brother in the eye.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Dragon Communion Seal** is a Sacred Seal in *Elden Ring*.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.markdown: Dropped by a spectral Banished Knight located in the Fringefolk Hero's Grave in Limgrave. To find it, start at the Stranded Graveyard Site of Grace and head down the first two ramps in the Grave, then head right in the split to go up another two ramps. The Knight is inside a small room at the end of the ramp and is quite tough for the early game. The Chariot in the dungeon can be used to help kill it, though that comes at considerable risk to the player as well.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- This Sacred Seal is best used for split Arcane/Faith builds, with an even split being slightly more favorable over one more biased towards Arcane. It can also be used for a pure Arcane build but that alternative is slightly weaker, by about 7-8%.
 - For comparison: a 45/45 Arc/Fth split gives 336 Scaling at +10, a 60/30 Arc/Fth split gives 333 Scaling at +10, and a 80/10 Arc/Fth split gives 310 Scaling at +10.
- Holding a Dragon Communion Seal (DCS) in one of your active hands will boost the damage of directly damaging Dragon Communion Incantations by 15%.
 - Holding a DCS in each active hand (that is, two Seals that are each held in separate hands) will increase the damage boost to 32.25% (1.15*1.15=1.3225).
 - The damage boost is still granted if the other piece of equipment is two-handed.
 - This bonus stacks with the 20% damage boost granted when reactivating the Rock Heart.
- Any incantation that inflicts Poison (except for Poison Armament), Madness, or non-bloodflame Blood Loss build-up and is cast using this Seal will have their Status Effect scale with the wielder's Arcane stat.
 - This status build-up bonus is equivalent to a fifth of the regular Weapon Scaling bonus from Stat Scaling, meaning that with a +10 DCS's scaling with Arcane being at 2.25 this caps at 45% (0.2*2.25=0.45).
 - Of the Blood Loss-inflicting incantations only Swarm of Flies inflicts any direct Blood Loss-build up (70 build-up out of its total 150 build-up) as direct status build-up instead of as part of a non-scaling bloodflame effect.
 - It would theoretically also scale the amount of Sleep build-up of any incantation that inflicts such a Status Effect. However, no incantation that inflicts that status effect exists.
 - Curiously Scarlet Rot build-up doesn't scale with Arcane, even though the spell type can inflict that status effect.
- The weight being 0 means and the existence of Physical Dragon Communion Incantations such as Dragonmaw and Rotten Breath means this Seal works well with the Blue Dancer Charm weight-based increase to Physical damage.
 - This synergy is further enhanced by the existence of the Rock Heart, essentially a 0 weight armor set that can increase the damage of Dragon Communion Incantations even further.
- This Seal is very unsuitable for casting Weapon Buff or direct healing spells as those depend entirely on the Faith portion of the used Seal's scaling, and this Seal only have about a third of the Faith scaling that pure Faith scaling Seals such as the Finger Seal and Erdtree Seal have.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.04 decreased the scaling of status effect build-up from spells and incantations of Albinauric Staff and Dragon Communion Seal.
 - Previously both of these casting implements full Arcane-scaling would apply to the Status Effects build-up of spells cast with them. For a +10 Dragon Communion Seal, this meant that almost the full S (2.25) would be applied thus resulting in roughly 3 times the Status Effect build-up on builds with high Arcane which would often result in instant or near instant application of Madness with spells such as Frenzied Burst.

sections.markdown: Daggers** are a type of melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Daggers generally have very short reach and low damage against both health and poise, but compensates for this with their fast attack speed and sometimes higher than average damage on Critical Attacks, making several of them (particularly the Dagger and especially the Misericorde) powerful tools for Backstabs and Ripostes.

Their fast attack-speed and high number of hits-per-second makes them good at building up Status Effects like Poison and Blood Loss.

As they have low weight, they also make excellent catalysts for certain Ashes of War and Skills, providing a stat-efficient means of casting status buffs like Golden Vow or Shared Order with no need for high investment in certain attributes, while specific daggers such as Reduvia and the Black Knife have exceptionally strong ranged Skills that only they posses (Reduvia Blood Blade and Blade of Death respectively).

sections.heading: Moveset
sections.markdown:
The moveset for Daggers consists mostly of rapid slashes, with the exception of one- and two-handed rolling and heavy running attacks, two-handed heavy attacks, and dual wield backstep attacks, which are all thrusts.

Some daggers have different standing heavy attacks: Glintstone Kris, Main-gauche, Miséricorde, and Scorpion's Stinger have thrusts, and Black Knife, Blade of Calling, Erdsteel Dagger, and Fire Knight's Shortsword have a quick, double-hit slash.

The dual-wield moveset is notably quite quick and both the backstep attack and the jumping attack are excellent due to their reach and speed respectively. The first attack in the dual-wield attack chain is surprisingly slow due to being composed of 3 separate hits, making it somewhat difficult to use since Daggers won't stagger most foes.

sections.markdown:
Discovery** is one of the stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Discovery affects their ability to find drops from defeated enemies. Discovery has a base level of 100 for the Tarnished, and Discovery can be raised by 1 for each point of Arcane taken while leveling up. Equipment can also boost Discovery while worn. Additionally, Discovery can be boosted temporarily by using a Silver-Pickled Fowl Foot consumbale item.

An item with a P% drop rate is actually found with probability as follows, if you have Discovery *D*:

 \begin{align}
Chance &= \frac{100\left \lfloor \frac{PD}{10} \right \rfloor}{1000+ \left \lfloor \frac{PD}{10} \right \rfloor-10P} \\
&= \frac{100}{1+\frac{1000-10P}{\left \lfloor \frac{PD}{10} \right \rfloor}} \\
&= \frac{10}{\frac{1}{10}+\frac{100-P}{\left \lfloor \frac{PD}{10} \right \rfloor}} \\
&\approx \frac{100}{1+\frac{10000-100P}{PD}} \\
\end{align}

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Demigods** (デミゴッド, *Demigoddo*) are special beings found in the Lands Between. They are the majority of the primary characters in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Lands Between are ruled by a family of demigods, heroes with an especially powerful blessing received from the blood of Queen Marika the Eternal. They are immortals due to their fated deaths being removed from the Elden Ring when Queen Marika created the Golden Order by sealing the Rune of Death.

During the Night of Black Knives, a fragment of the Rune of Death enabled the murder of Godwyn the Golden. This was the first death of a demigod in all history, and it was after this that the demigods began to fall. At an unknown period, Queen Marika told her demigod children to make of themselves that which they desired, whether it be a Lord, or a God. However, she also declared that if they failed to become anything at all, they would be forsaken, and amount only to a sacrifice.

These events were precursors to the shattering of the Elden Ring, whereupon several of the demigods inherited Great Runes, becoming known as Shardbearers. The mad taint of the strength granted by their Great Runes triggered the Shattering, a war in which the demigods fought for control of the Lands Between. However, no lord arose from the Shattering, and the demigods were abandoned by the Greater Will.

Upon their return to the Lands Between, the Tarnished were impelled by the Two Fingers to seek out the demigods and relieve them of their Great Runes. At least three of the demigods were slain by The Tarnished in their quest to become Elden Lord.

sections.heading: The Golden Lineage
sections.markdown:
The first Demigods were Godfrey, First Elden Lord and his descendants, known as the Golden Lineage. The confirmed members of the Golden Lineage are Morgott, the Omen King, his twin Mohg, Lord of Blood, Godrick the Grafted, Godefroy the Grafted, and the Grafted Scions. Godwyn the Golden's name, title, and the pattern on his clothing suggests his descendancy from the Golden Lineage.

Godrick the Grafted was only a distant relation, his divine blood linking him to Marika sorely diluted, indicating unseen generations of Golden Lineage demigods. According to Kenneth Haight, Godrick is the last of the Golden Lineage, but the Grafted Scions are also suggested to be the dregs of the Golden Lineage.

When Godfrey was divested of his Grace, he became Tarnished, and lost his demigod status.

sections.heading: Carian Royal Family
sections.markdown: After Godfrey was hounded from the Lands Between, Radagon became King Consort and second Elden Lord by marrying Queen Marika. This led to the children he conceived with Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon becoming demigod stepchildren, including Starscourge Radahn, Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy, and Ranni the Witch.

sections.heading: Messmer and Melina
sections.markdown:
Messmer and Melina are both children of Marika.
- It is often speculated that the Kindling Maiden Melina may be a demigod, as she is called "DaughterMarika" internally and states her mother is inside the Erdtree. Furthermore, she is bound by Grace, quotes ancient words of Marika, and implied to be the younger sister of Messmer the Impaler. Like Messmer, Melina is associated with a butterfly and is fated to fulfill a purpose.

sections.heading: Twin Prodigies
sections.markdown: The union of Radagon and Marika led to the birth of at least two more demigods, the twins Miquella of the Haligtree and Malenia, Blade of Miquella, however they suffered afflictions from birth; the former was born with a curse of eternal childhood, and the latter harbored Scarlet Rot within.

sections.heading: Soulless Demigods
sections.markdown: The Wandering Mausoleums found throughout the Lands Between cradle the corpses of soulless demigods. At least eight demigods became these soulless demigods, and at least one of them is an unwanted child of Queen Marika's. They are guarded by the Mausoleum Knights, who watch over a soulless demigod until their resurrection.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- According to Finger Reader Enia, the demigods are each and all the direct offspring of Queen Marika.
- According to the Overview Trailer, the demigods are "those who have inherited the blood of Queen Marika the Eternal."

As part of the creative process, Martin wrote the initial characters as grand heroes, and FromSoftware took them developed the way in which their Great Runes misshaped and distorted them.

The art of perfuming, once jealously guarded within the Royal Capital, became widespread as the wars raged on. Unlike their white-robed counterparts, their aprons were embroidered with intertwining serpents, said to be a curse upon the Erdtree.

Depraved Perfumers practiced forbidden arts, such as Acid Spraymist, Poison Spraymist, and Bloodboil Aromatic, and were in league with Living Jar poachers.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Demi-humans** are enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Demi-Humans are typically small in stature and bestial in appearance, often possessing fur, canine faces, and pointed ears. Although they are intelligent and capable of speech, as exemplified by Boc the Seamster, they are typically violent and brutish, particularly at night when their blood boils and they turn feral.

Demi-Humans wield a variety of weapons, such as falchions, daggers, and clubs. Those considered to be the toughest wield spiked clubs, which they believe to be a badge of honor.

Demi-Human society appears to be hierarchical, with the lesser Demi-Humans following much larger Demi-Human Chiefs. Demi-Humans lose hope if their leader dies, causing them to panic and stop attacking. At the top of the Demi-Human hierarchy are the Queens, who are capable of wielding rudimentary sorceries via their staves.

Despite their violent demeanour, Demi-Humans are capable of fostering diplomatic relations with humans, with Kenneth Haight building an alliance with a group of Demi-Humans in Fort Haight.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: Demi-humans of average build, who wear rags. Demi-humans are bestial in appearance, often characterized by fur, elongated faces, and pointed ears. They exhibit a blend of human and mammalian features, yet all share the common trait of possessing five fingers and toes. While typically shorter than the Tarnished, demi-humans vary greatly in size—some are as small as children while others are of towering stature. Demi-humans wield a variety of weapons, including falchions and clubs; some carry rickety shields. Many demi-humans carry string. As night falls, demi-humans become increasingly feral and aggressive, their eyes glowing a menacing red.

Dexterity** is one of the main attribute stats in Elden Ring.

The Tarnished's Dexterity stat affects which weapons they can wield effectively and affects the damage output of weapons which have Dexterity scaling. Increasing Dexterity will also decreased the Tarnished's casting time with spells as it raises. Fall damage will also be reduced as Dexterity raises past 21 Dexterity.

The Tarnished can level Dexterity by spending Runes at Sites of Grace.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Dragons are the mortal descendants of the Ancient Dragons, who once ruled the Lands Between during a prehistoric era. Unlike their predecessors, their fleshy hides bore no Gravel Stone scales. They possessed fewer limbs and flew on feathered wings. Their snouts were more narrow and terminated in diminutive maxillary beaks.

The dragons were idolized by humans for their sheer strength and sublime beauty. However, the ancient dragons viewed them as lowborn, paltry imitations. While the drakes inherited the fiery breath of their forebears, they could not channel their red lightning. Yet, their vivacious red hearts were covered in sacred gravel stones.

Well before the first astrologers and the Erdtree, ice dragons held dominion over the Mountaintops. Some time later, they were defeated by the Fire Giants, who drove them the Flame Peak.

Many dragons in the current age descend from Elder Dragon Greyoll, a mother drake of colossal size. Following the Battle of Aeonia, Greyoll and her offspring fled the Scarlet Rot by settling on a plateau in the northern reaches of Caelid, later known as Greyoll's Dragonbarrow.

sections.heading: Flying Dragon
sections.markdown:
Flying Dragon Description
Dragons who settled in northern Caelid with their mother, Elder Dragon Greyoll.

- There are six red-eyed Flying Dragons surrounding Greyoll. Greyoll will lose 20% of her health with each Dragon killed, meaning that killing five will cause Greyoll to die.

sections.heading: Glintstone Dragon
sections.markdown:
Glintstone Dragon Description
Dragons imbued with glintstone roost atop the Moonlight Altar in western Liurnia of the Lakes. They can exhale Glintstone Breath, which inflicts magic damage.

- These Dragons do not respawn when killed.

sections.heading: Flying Dragon Agheel
sections.markdown:
Flying Dragon Agheel Overview
Wandering Nobles in the ruins around the lake chant Agheel's name, praying that it will burn them to ash. Flying Dragon Agheel is encountered in Agheel Lake in southern Limgrave, northwest of the Dragon-Burnt Ruins. It appears by flying down from above, torching a congregation of Wandering Nobles with dragonfire.

- Bloody Finger Hunter Yura is available as a summon for this fight, after speaking to him under the ruin south of the lake.

- After taking a critical hit, the target receives an additional 20% standard damage for the remainder of the fight.

- Defeating Flying Dragon Agheel will unlock Agheel's Flame, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for two Dragon Hearts.
Moveset

sections.heading: Flying Dragon Greyll
sections.markdown:
Flying Dragon Greyll Overview
A Flying Dragon encountered on the Farum Greatbridge (bridge south of Bestial Sanctum), on the northern peninsula of Greyoll's Dragonbarrow. Greyll is identical to Agheel in both appearance and ability. However, the bridge gives the player much less room to maneuver.
Moveset

sections.heading: Glintstone Dragon Smarag
sections.markdown:
Glintstone Dragon Smarag Overview
A devourer of sorcerers, whose body gradually became corrupted by the glintstones of those he ate. Smarag is encountered near an island west of the Academy of Raya Lucaria and north of the Temple Quarter, guarding a corpse that holds the Academy Glintstone Key. Note that it is **not** necessary to kill this dragon to get the Academy Glintstone Key; it can be retrieved by either sneaking behind it or rushing beyond it before it's fully awakened to get at the corpse.

- Smarag is able to fire Glintstone Cometshards from his mouth, and can also unleash magic breath, akin to the fire breath of other Dragons.

- Defeating Glintstone Dragon Smarag will unlock Smarag's Glintstone Breath, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for two Dragon Hearts.
Moveset

sections.heading: Glintstone Dragon Adula
sections.markdown:
Glintstone Dragon Adula Overview
A devourer of sorcerers, whose body became corrupted by glintstone. Adula was once bested by Ranni the Witch and subsequently swore a knightly oath to her Dark Moon.

- Adula is first encountered outside Ranni's Rise in the Three Sisters, north of Caria Manor. After a brief fight, it disappears, only to reappear at the Moonlight Altar outside the Cathedral of Manus Celes.

- Adula can use magic breath, much like Smarag. However, it can also utilize Adula's Moonblade, conjuring a magic blade in its maw mid-flight and unleashing a wave that inflicts Frostbite.
Moveset

sections.heading: Decaying Ekzykes
sections.markdown:
A Dragon plagued by scarlet rot, encountered north-west of the Cathedral of Dragon Communion. Also known as the **Dragon Communion Revenger**, Ekzykes did not forget his hatred even as he succumbed to the rot.

Instead of flames, Ekzykes breathes toxic clouds that inflict Scarlet Rot, covering a large area and taking a few seconds to dissipate. Its stomps also produce a small cloud of Scarlet Rot.

Defeating Decaying Ekzykes will unlock Ekzykes's Decay, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for two Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Borealis the Freezing Fog
sections.markdown:
One of the ice dragons, who were lords of the Mountaintops before the Fire Giants chased them from the peak. Borealis is encountered on the frozen lake in the northeast of the Mountaintops, emerging from a thick white fog.

Borealis exhales clouds that inflict Frostbite. Its stomps also produce small clouds of Frostbite.

Defeating Borealis the Freezing Fog will unlock Borealis's Mist, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for two Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Elder Dragon Greyoll
sections.markdown:
Greyoll is known as the mother of the lesser dragons. She is a massive but stationary dragon encountered in Greyoll's Dragonbarrow, just south of Fort Faroth. She is immobile, either having grown too weak to move or as a result of having fused with the surrounding rocks, but can still let loose fearsome roars to weaken her enemies.

- Defeating any of the six lesser dragons surrounding her will cause large amounts of damage to her, and killing them all will kill her.

- Defeating Elder Dragon Greyoll will unlock Greyoll's Roar, which can be obtained at the altar in the Cathedral of Dragon Communion in Caelid for three Dragon Hearts.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
An ancient structure in a deep ravine in northern Caelid. Inside is a lift which connects Caelid to Siofra River. As the ravine is inaccessible from the rest of Caelid, the only way to access this area is by taking the lift up from beside the Below the River Well Site of Grace in northeastern Siofra River, requiring two Stonesword Keys to activate it.

The ravine branches in two directions from the well. Travelling south will lead to a one-way drop to the Swamp of Aeonia, while the western path leads to the Great Jar and the Caelid Colosseum.

sections.heading: Walkthrough
sections.markdown:
Upon entering the Dragonbarrow location several passive Standing Sentry Stones will be found crowding the path, while Explosive ones dot the lower parts. Just around a corner is a Golem with a magical greatbow guarding the way, with another waiting far behind it to support. Since the second Golem will attack you when near the Great Jar and the first one will you near the second golem, it is best to take care of both before approaching.

Additionally, Gravel Stones dot the ground just before the stone the first Golem is standing on.

For the encounter with the gigantic Living Jar at the end, see the Great Jar page.

sections.markdown: Dominula, Windmill Village** is a location in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Dominula is a village situated on a hill in the northern Altus Plateau, north of the Woodfolk Ruins. A number of wooden crosses shaped like Marika's Rune and adorned with pink floral wreathes are erected around the village. Flowers also rest on the heads of the villagers, who wear white robes stained with dried blood. The celebrants dance barefoot beneath the windmills, twirling in place as part of their ancient tradition.

Most of the dancers are too caught up in the festivities to attack the player. Those who are not dancing will attack on sight, however, and will alert the rest of the villagers to attack. The eyes of many villagers glow red. On the south side of the village, a Stranded Soul cowers in fear of a festive melody, pleading to not be skinned.

At the top of the hill upon which the village stands is a Godskin Apostle, a member of a group that once hunted and flayed the gods.

sections.markdown: Dominula Dancers**, also known as **Celebrants**, are Enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Joyous Dominula Dancers twirl barefoot beneath the windmills in northern Altus Plateau, their skin and clothing caked with dried blood. The maidens of Dominula, Windmill Village and its surrounding pastures have gathered to celebrate an old festival to which Queen Marika paid a blind eye. Each wears a crown of many-colored flowers and wields a ritual implement blessed to draw in the power of runes. The young girls in vibrant blue capes played a central role by separating sacrifices from their skin.

Celebrants are smiling woman with elongated fingers, gold-colored eyes, and silver hair, worn in two braids—one long and the other cut short. Dressed in filthy clothing, some don yellow or blue hooded capes embroidered with designs associated with the Erdtree and Godskin Apostles, respectively. They wear crowns of pink and violet flowers, golden linchpins, and large amulets with six gold spheres orbiting a central orb. Their ceremonial weapons and festival grease are fashioned from human bones decorated with vibrant flowers and fabrics. Some wield hefty clubs made from the skulls of giants, though the blue maidens exclusively use daggers and the Celebrant's Sickle.

Dominula Dancers laugh and chatter peacefully while they dance, seemingly oblivious to the player. However, they draw their weapons and become hostile if one of them is attacked. Celebrants sometimes bite their wrists and attack by spewing their own blood.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: There are several Damage Types in Elden Ring, divided by being either Physical or Elemental.

sections.heading: Physical damage types
sections.markdown:
- Standard is the damage dealt by attacks that are neither particularly sharp, nor heavy, nor thin, such as those from Axes and Straight Swords.
- Strike is the damage dealt by heavy and blunt attacks, such as those from Hammers and many Colossal Weapons.
- Slash is the damage dealt by sharp attacks, such as those from Claws and Curved Swords.
- Pierce is the damage dealt by thrusting attacks, such as those from Thrusting Swords and Spears. They have the additional benefit of dealing increased damage against attacking foes.

sections.heading: Non-Physical damage types
sections.markdown:
- Fire is the damage dealt by flaming attacks, and are common among Incantations and Torches.
- Holy is the damage dealt by bright golden attacks, and are common among Incantations and Weapons associated with the Erdtree, the various Two Fingers, and the Rune of Death.
- Lightning is the damage dealt by attacks that sparkle with yellow or red lightning, and are common among Incantations and weapons associated with Ancient Dragons.
- Magic is the damage dealt by Frostbite-based and blue or turqoise attacks, and are most common among Sorceries.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown:
Dragon Cult incantations** are a type of incantation in Elden Ring. These spells are characterized by their use of lightning and their association with the ancient dragons. They typically require a moderate to high Faith Attribute to cast.

The Gravel Stone Seal boosts the damage of these spells by 15% when held in an active hand (32.25% if one is held in each hand), not including Electrify Armament as it is a Weapon Buff spell.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
An enormous ancient dragon named Gransax once assaulted the Erdtree in ancient times. The knights of the Erdtree fortified themselves with lightning as they fought in what would later be known as the War of the Ancient Dragons.

The war ended when Godwyn the Golden defeated the ancient dragon Fortissax. The demigod was said to have befriended his fallen foe, and their bond eventually led to the formation of a ancient dragon cult within Leyndell, Royal Capital. The ancient dragons took the form of humans to teach them their lightning incantations. Only the highest-ranking members of the order knew of the dragon's red lightning.

The malformed Dragonkin Soldiers of the Eternal Cities wielded a blue ice lightning.

sections.heading: Boosting Dragon Cult incantations
sections.markdown:
Lightning Scorpion Charm increases Lightning Attack Power by 12% (8% in PvP).
- Lightning-Shrouding Cracked Tear increases Lightning Attack Power by 20% (15% in PvP) for 3 minutes. 
- Gravel Stone Seal increases Lightning Attack Power by 15% when held in an active hand, and by 32.5% when wielded in each hand. 
 - The Gravel Stone Seal bonus does not apply to Electrify Armament, as it applies a weapon Buff.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown: - A yellow sigil appears for yellow lightning spells, a red sigil for red lightning spells, and a blue sigil for ice lightning spells.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The divine beasts were messengers of the heavens. The sculpted keepers are representations used to perform the ritual of the lion dance during the tower festival in Belurat, Tower Settlement. Only the greatest of horned warriors became divine beast warriors, and few became sculpted keepers.

When Messmer the Impaler's army assailed the tower, the lion dance was turned towards martial ends.. By the end of Messmer's Crusade, only two divine beasts remained: one inside of Belurat, and another in the Ancient Ruins of Rauh. The one in Belurat was under the control of Hornsent Grandam, who directed the divine beast to rest until the Impaler's forces returned so it could exact vengeance for her people. When a Tarnished Champion happened upon the divine beast's resting place, Grandam assumed them to be one of Messmer's prodigies and ordered the divine beast to slay the Tarnished. It failed to do so, however, and was slain. The Tarnished can also encounter and slay the other divine beasts while exploring Rauh, thereby putting an end to them.

sections.heading: Boss Fight

The Divine Beast will fight normally in its first phase. Around 70% health, it will switch between three storm-based elements on a timed basis: Lightning, Frost, and Wind.

The Divine Beast Dancing Lion at the Ancient Ruins of Rauh also has access to Death Blight.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: is a historical practice in Elden Ring. It involves the hunting of drakes, the descendants of Ancient Dragons, in pursuit of their gravel stone-covered hearts. Specifically, *Dragon Communion* is the act of consuming dragon hearts to acquire the draconic powers within. The hearts are consumed at a Dragon Communion Altar, which is usually in the presence of a fallen dragon.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
In the distant past, the lord of the ancient dragons, Placidusax, was attacked by the great drake, Bayle the Dread. Their clash ended in a stalemate and left both gravely injured, with Bayle fleeing the field of battle. As vengeance for Bayle's transgression, Placidusax had some of his followers take mortal forms as humanoid priestesses and travel to the lands of men, where they would beckon human warriors to their cause. They established the practice of dragon communion to hunt down and punish Bayle and his descendants, the drakes. The human warriors were lured to this cause with the promise of great power, which could only be acquired by consuming the heart of a drake.

As time passed, the practice continued without the priestesses' influence; however, many practitioners forgot the original purpose of these hunts and continued consuming hearts for personal gain. Many practitioners develop a hunger for hearts as they hunt, which gradually intensifies the more hearts they devour. This leads many to commune without restraint, an act that has dire consequences for their humanity, as their bodies and minds gradually become increasingly draconic. The result is transformation into Magma Wyrms, dragon-like creatures with pitifully small wings, incapable of flight, and cursed to crawl the earth on their bellies until the end of their days. Ironically, this end often comes at the hands of their fellow communers as their own hearts are now a sufficient target for dragon communion as well.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Count Ymir, High Priest**, later known as the boss **Ymir, Mother of Fingers**, is a character in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Count Ymir is located at the Cathedral of Manus Metyr on the eastern Scadu Altus in the Realm of Shadow. He may be found sitting on his throne during the day but spends his nights in the attached graveyard visiting his son Yuri. Ymir offers cryptic guidance and items to aid those who seek their purpose. He provides the player with a map to a hallowed ruin, claiming it holds the key to fate guided by the stars.

Count Ymir is protected by his loyal Swordhands of Night: Jolán and her sister, Anna.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Count Ymir was a master glintstone sorcerer renowned for his understanding of the cosmos. During the time of Elden Lord Godfrey, he served the Carian Royals and taught glintstone sorcery to Rellana, Twin Moon Knight. With a wizened hand gently gripping a glintstone, he often inspired his students, saying, "One need only envision the romance of the stars above with adoration for stardust in one's heart to become a great sorcerer. Do so, and you will know love." Although he originally held allegiance to the moons, he eventually dismissed them in his pursuit of deeper cosmic truths.

Ymir uncovered secrets of the Greater Will during expedition into the hallowed Finger Ruins in the eastern Realm of Shadow. He studied the lamprey that dwelled within and mastered their Finger Sorcery, becoming a Finger-Weaver. Below the Cathedral of Manus Metyr, he found the Finger Ruins of Miyr concealed the Finger Birthing Grounds, where Metyr waited in vain.

Ymir learned that Metyr's true power and the guidance of the Two Fingers had been broken long ago. He became the high priest of Manus Metyr and acquired the service of the Swordhands of Night. After his child, Yuri, died at a tender age, Ymir's grief drove him to find a way to bring him back. He decided he would succeed Metyr as the next mother of Fingers. He began ingesting Fingerprint Nostrum and birthing Fingercreepers of his own.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.markdown: Ymir shares the wisdom of the cosmos and a Hole-Laden Necklace with the Tarnished champion. He directs them to sound the ominous hanging bells at the Finger Ruins of Dheo and Rhia. Once both bells are rung, Ymir reveals the location of the Ruins of Miyr. Ringing the third and final bell will leave one's fate guided by the stars—and face-to-face with Metyr. If the Mother of Fingers is defeated, Ymir's hope is rekindled but the prospect of achieving his dream drives him mad. He achieves a partial transformation and fails to birth Yuri anew, instead creating more Fingercreepers.
